cards.title: Exact spectral resolvent: integrating before the modulus is valid
cards.actual: Weighted.md replaces separate endpoint/integral moduli with the signed primitive’s integrated zero term. No frozen Lean declaration proves that spectral integration; the prose explicitly says so.
cards.primary_claim: GM Eq. (1.3a), page 2, with Lemma 3.3, page 9, gives the following K=Q primitive. The completed-zeta Hadamard product and functional equation used for the mass calculation are GM (3.3)–(3.6), page 7.
cards.analysis: For each primitive zero term, the signed boundary and integrated term combine algebraically into −1/[ρ(1+s−ρ)]; the r′ constant cancels. Absolute interchange can be justified before this cancellation: the two terms from the primitive are bounded by [1+(2+s)/(s+1/2)]x⁻¹ᐟ²⁻ˢ/|ρ(ρ+1)|, with bracket at most 5 for s≥0. Thus the convergent inverse-square mass dominates them uniformly. RH gives 1−ρ=conjugate(ρ), and |1+s−ρ|²=|ρ|²+s+s². Subtracting the completed Hadamard logarithmic derivatives at 1 and 0 gives the absolutely convergent mass; the completed function is nonzero at those points, so the zeta pole has been removed. The digamma value at 1/2 and the Laurent coefficient at 1 give 2+γ−log(4π). Elementary bounds γ<.578 and log(4π)>2.531 are independently checked. For the trivial term, −log(1−t⁻²)/2≤(9/16)t⁻², so its positive contribution is smaller than the subtracted log(2π) term. Finally, the Laplace representation of 1/log t+1/log²t permits the s integral, with absolute integrability supplied by Schoenfeld.
cards.impact: Accepted written RH mathematics with exact source normalization and justified interchanges. It uses no numerical zero list. It remains outside the frozen Lean proof chain and is not source-first program verification.
